poster_title: Crossing the Reward Bridge: Expanding RL with Verifiable Rewards Across Diverse Domains
authors: Yi Su, Dian Yu, Linfeng Song, Juntao Li, Haitao Mi, Zhaopeng Tu, Min Zhang, and Dong Yu

panels.headline: Expanding RLVR to diverse, less structured domains
content: RLVR has shown success in enhancing LLMs' performance in structured tasks.
Binary verification signals are used in structured answer scenarios.
Challenges in verifying unstructured answers in diverse domains.
Lack of ground-truth labels complicates the verification process.
Need for a more flexible and robust RLVR framework.

panels.headline: Verifying complex, unstructured answers
content: Traditional RLVR methods are limited to structured tasks.
Unstructured domains lack clear reference answers.
Need for a new approach to handle diverse and complex tasks.
Cross-domain verification requires robust and flexible models.
Soft rewards can provide more nuanced feedback.

panels.headline: Generative model-based soft rewards
content: Propose a framework incorporating generative model-based soft rewards.
Compute soft rewards from a single indicative token's probability.
Train compact cross-domain generative reward models using noisy datasets.
Integrate the framework into RLVR for enhanced performance.
panels.figure_caption: Overview paradigm of RLVR with our cross-domain verifier.

panels.headline: Comprehensive experiments across diverse domains
content: Evaluate the framework in medicine, chemistry, psychology, economics, and education.
Use free-form, unstructured answer scenarios for testing.
Collect noisy datasets during RL exploration for training.
Demonstrate the feasibility of training compact models.
panels.figure_caption: Example question and reference answer pairs in ExamQA.

panels.headline: Performance boosts of up to 8.0% accuracy
content: Significantly outperform state-of-the-art open-source aligned models.
Achieve up to 8.0% accuracy improvement in diverse reasoning tasks.
Show robust performance across different domains and tasks.
Empirically validate the effectiveness of the framework.
panels.figure_caption: Performance Comparison of Different Methods. Base model: Qwen2.5-7B. E: elementary. M: middle. H: high.

panels.headline: Enhanced robustness, flexibility, and scalability
content: Extended RLVR framework improves performance in complex, noisy-label scenarios.
Generative, model-based soft rewards show promise for broader applications.
Released a dataset and trained reward model to facilitate future research.
Potential for further improvements and applications in unstructured domains.
